Figure 2: Evidence from Within-Country Changes over Time

For the y-axis: Total Fertility Rate is taken from the World Development Indicator SP.DYN.TFRT.IN (World Bank 2025). For the x-axis, panel A: Human Capital Index from Barro and Lee (2013). Panel B: real GDP per capita from the World Development Indicator NY.GDP.PCAP.CD. Panel C: Child mortality is defined as the probability (per 1,000 live births) that a newborn will die before reaching age five, based on the World Development Indicator SH.DYN.MORT. Panel D: Maternal mortality ratio is the estimated number of women who die from pregnancy-related causes while pregnant or within 42 days of pregnancy termination per 100,000 live births, taken from the World Development Indicator SH.STA.MMRT.
Time period: 1960 and 2010. Data on maternal mortality are not available prior to 1985.
